name: Assess hazards before each job
summary: Before every cementing or coiled tubing job, and at the start of every shift on a fracturing pad, the field supervisor walks the site, writes a field level hazard assessment (high pressure lines, H2S, overhead lifts, traffic and sand haul, simultaneous operations, weather) with the controls for each hazard, and runs a safety meeting where the crew discusses and signs it, often with the customer's wellsite supervisor. Alberta law requires a dated written assessment before work begins and again when the work changes, with the workers involved. The paper forms travel back to the base with the job package, are filed with the job and summarised for the HSE group, and field HSE advisors check a sample. The common failures are copied or generic assessments, missed reassessment when conditions change, and forms that are filed late or lost.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with about 880 field staff in fracturing, cementing and coiled tubing crews working on customer leases in Alberta and northeast BC.
baseline.notes: Paper field level hazard assessment books with carbon copies were the common practice; some crews used tablet forms. Summaries keyed into the HSE system by a coordinator.

unit_of_work: one field level hazard assessment (one job, or one shift on a fracturing pad)
trigger: A crew is about to start a job or a shift: a cementing or coiled tubing job from a dispatch order, or a shift on a fracturing pad program.
end_state: The signed assessment is used at the site, filed with the job and summarised in the HSE system.

volume.seasonality: Follows field activity: highest January to March, lowest in spring break-up and in 2020.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume kept. Check: seven frac crews x two shifts x about 30 days = about 420; about 450 cementing jobs; about 80 coiled tubing jobs x 3-4 shifts plus about 60 nitrogen jobs = about 340; total about 1,200 in a busy month.

steps.name: Route the assessment to the service line
steps.description: Not a work step: the dispatch order or the pad program's shift schedule decides which supervisor and crew carry out the assessment, using that service line's field level hazard assessment form.

next.condition: coiled tubing or nitrogen job or shift

evidence.note: Shares from the volume check in the volume note.

steps.name: Review the fracturing job and site requirements
steps.description: The fracturing supervisor reads the program or dispatch order, the customer's site safety requirements and emergency response plan, the previous shift's assessment and any hazard alerts, and notes pressure zones around the treating iron, sand haul traffic, wireline and other crews on the pad.

error.defect_description: Copies the previous assessment instead of reviewing what has changed.

evidence.note: TRACK hazard management steps (trican-esg) and the OHS Code requirement (ab-ohs-code-p2). Times tier C.

steps.name: Walk the site and write the assessment
steps.description: The supervisor walks the lease and the work area, checks wind direction, gas monitors, muster point, exclusion zones around pressurised lines and traffic routes, and writes each task, its hazards, risk and controls on the dated field level hazard assessment form.

error.defect_description: Generic or incomplete hazards and controls written, not specific to the site.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code s.7 hazard assessment before work begins (BC OHS Regulation in BC)

next.condition: a hazard cannot be controlled as planned

evidence.note: OHS Code s.7 requires a dated written hazard assessment before work begins and when work changes; s.8 requires worker participation. Times tier C.

steps.name: Stop work and fix the uncontrolled hazard
steps.description: The supervisor uses stop-work authority, calls the customer's wellsite supervisor and, where needed, the operations manager or HSE advisor, and agrees a fix such as moving equipment, waiting for wind or daylight, more gas monitoring or isolating the other operation, before reassessing.

control.basis: Company refuse-unsafe-work commitment and OHS Act right to refuse dangerous work

evidence.note: Commitment to refuse unsafe work and know when to continue (TRACK). Share and time tier C.

steps.name: Lead the safety meeting
steps.description: The supervisor gathers the crew on shift, reads through the tasks, hazards and controls, assigns roles such as spotter and gas tester, reviews the emergency plan and asks each person for hazards they see, adding them to the form.

steps.name: Customer wellsite supervisor reviews and signs
steps.description: The customer's wellsite supervisor attends or reads the assessment, checks it covers the customer's site rules and the other contractors on the lease, and signs or initials it; some customers keep a copy.

control.basis: Customer contractor safety requirements on its leases (prime contractor)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: HSE advisor checks the assessment on site
steps.description: On a site visit the field HSE advisor reads the day's assessment against the work going on, checks that hazards are specific and controls are in place, talks to crew members about it, and records the check and any findings.

control.basis: Company safety management system field inspections (COR audit evidence)

evidence.note: Safety management system and tracking of hazard identification; sample share and finding rate tier C.

steps.name: Coach the supervisor and record the finding
steps.description: The advisor goes through the weak assessment with the supervisor, shows what a site-specific entry looks like, has it corrected for the rest of the job, and logs an audit finding when the gap is serious or repeated.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: File the assessment with the job package
steps.description: When the job paperwork comes back to the base with the crew or the field ticket, the district administrator checks the form is signed and dated, scans it to the job folder or attaches it to the ticket for customers who require it, and files the paper copy.

error.defect_description: Form missing or unsigned, not chased.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Key the summary into the HSE system
steps.description: The HSE coordinator enters each filed assessment's site, date, crew, hazard categories and stop-work events into the HSE system for monthly leading-indicator reports and audit sampling, and lists missing forms by crew.

error.defect_description: Keying error in hazard category or date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB coiled tubing and pressure pumping field practice in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Uncontrolled hazard stops work
exceptions.description: A hazard such as wind direction for H2S, an overhead line or another crew's operation cannot be controlled as planned; work stops until a fix is agreed.

exceptions.name: Reassessment when work changes
exceptions.description: The job changes (new task, weather, simultaneous operation) and the supervisor rewrites the assessment with the crew.

exceptions.name: Weak assessment found
exceptions.description: An HSE advisor finds a copied or generic assessment and coaches the supervisor; repeated gaps become audit findings.

evidence.note: No published figure. Rests on paper forms returning with job packages at the end of a job or rotation and weekly to monthly keying. The time from start of assessment to start of work is 30-90 minutes.

evidence.note: Sum of the review, walk and meeting steps in this file.

pain_points.description: Assessments are copied from the previous shift or written generically, so site-specific hazards are missed; this is a common audit finding.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description; general knowledge of COR audit findings.

pain_points.description: Paper forms take days to come back to the base and some are lost, so the HSE group sees hazards and stop-work events late.

evidence.note: General knowledge of paper form handling in the period.

sources.title: Trican - ESG
sources.supports: Employees trained in the TRACK hazard management program (understand the task, recognise hazards, assess risks, control risks, know when to continue); commitment to refuse unsafe work; Safety Management System with training and mentoring until workers are competent; Target Zero incident goal and tracking of hazard identification.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code, Part 2: Hazard Assessment, Elimination and Control
sources.supports: Section 7: employer assesses the work site and identifies existing and potential hazards before work begins, prepares a dated report of the assessment and the control methods, and repeats it at reasonably practicable intervals, when a new work process is introduced, when a work process or operation changes, and before significant site alterations. Section 8: affected workers must be involved in the hazard assessment and in controlling the hazards.

assumptions: Loaded cost per hour comes from the organisation file (base wage x 1.35).
Step s01 is a routing step with no work, so that each service line's supervisor and crew are shown separately.
The crew step stands for everyone on shift in that service line; frac-pump-operator stands for the whole frac crew.
The crew's meeting time is counted here, not in the job execution workflows.
Crew roles, district administrator and HSE coordinator take part but are not in the process map's role list.
BC jobs follow the BC OHS Regulation, which also requires hazard identification and worker involvement; the Alberta rule is cited because most work is in Alberta.
